Subject: Packaging mapping & floor/clawback — need clarification

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the chat earlier. As we review the draft Order Schedule (attached), our procurement team needs a clear mapping between the SKU-level packaging definitions and the pricing floor/clawback mechanics. Two specific asks: 

- Confirm how usage across multiple SKUs maps into the "banded" floors and whether SKUs can be aggregated for the floor calculation.
- Clarify the clawback trigger: is it per-sku, per-band, or at the account aggregate? The current language in Exhibit B is ambiguous and procurement will not sign without explicit examples.

I've attached Acme_Order_Schedule_v3.xlsx with the SKU mapping we use; you can see how test/dev SKUs and production SKUs are interleaved in our billing.

Can your team propose redline language that (a) defines aggregation rules, (b) provides a single worked example, and (c) includes a seasonal variance carveout? We need this for our internal approval by next Wednesday.

Thanks,
Amanda Cole
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Health

Amanda — thanks for the clear asks and the sample mapping. Looping in Laura, Karthik and Marissa to draft language. Summary of next steps from our side: 

1) Legal (Karthik) to propose a definition for "Billable Unit" and whether aggregation is allowed across SKUs for the floor calculation.
2) Pricing (Laura & Marissa) to propose a smoothing approach that avoids cliffed clawbacks while preserving revenue protection.
3) We'll return a redlined Exhibit B with an attached worked example and a seasonal variance carveout.

Preliminary thought from Sales: we can offer two acceptable patterns for you to choose from — (A) Account-aggregate floors (single floor computed across all production SKUs; test/dev SKUs excluded by label), or (B) Per-SKU floors with an aggregation override for <5 SKUs. Option A is simpler for procurement but requires clearer labeling of what counts as "production." Option B is more surgical but slightly more operational.

I attached a quick annotated PDF (redline_markup_v1.pdf) with line notes for context; legal/pricing will formalize.

I'll aim to get the redline back by EOD today for an internal pass and then to you tomorrow morning.

Subject: Re: Packaging mapping & floor/clawback — draft legal markup

Priyom / Team — see inline legal suggestions below. I focused on two risk points: definition/aggregation and the clawback trigger window. Suggested redlines (high level):

1) Define "Billable Unit": "Billable Unit means the product unit that is measured for billing as set forth in the Order Schedule. For avoidance of doubt, Billable Units may be labeled as 'production' or 'non-production' in the SKU mapping; only production-labeled Billable Units shall count toward floor calculations unless the parties otherwise agree in writing."

2) Aggregation rule: "Unless explicitly specified in the Order Schedule, the floor and clawback calculations shall be performed at the Account aggregate across all production Billable Units. Parties may opt into per-SKU floors by listing the applicable SKUs in an appendix to the Order Schedule."

3) Clawback trigger and window: "A clawback shall only apply where measured Billable Units fall below eighty percent (80%) of the forecasted Account aggregate for three (3) consecutive billing months, as specified in the forecast attached to the Order Schedule. Excluded from this calculation are months where variance is attributable to seasonal demand (as supported by historical usage) or force majeure events."

4) Worked example: include a small table in Exhibit B showing aggregation across 3 SKUs with a sample true-up calculation.

See attached pricing_exhibit_markup.docx for line-by-line edits. Two notes for Pricing: we should decide whether the 80% / 3-month window is acceptable or if we want a 70%/2-month option for smaller customers.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: pricing_exhibit_markup.docx (word)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Packaging mapping & floor/clawback — pricing perspective

Thanks Karthik — clear framing. From a pricing operations perspective, two small edits to reduce churn and avoid cliff outcomes: 

- Propose a smoothing band so clawback is proportional rather than binary. Suggested language: "When measured usage is between 60%-80% of forecast for the 3-month rolling window, the clawback amount shall be calculated on a pro rata basis using a linear interpolation between 0% (at 80%) and 100% (at 60%)."

- Seasonal carveout mechanics: rather than a blanket exclusion, require the customer to supply historical month-over-month seasonality tags in the Order Schedule. If a month is tagged as seasonal and usage variance is within the historical seasonal range, that month is excluded from the consecutive months count.

Also recommend we explicitly exclude dev/test SKUs by name pattern (e.g., suffix "-dev" or label in the SKU sheet) so ops does not have to apply manual filters on every invoice.

I'll prepare suggested exhibit language and an alternative worked example (account-aggregate vs per-SKU) and attach it to the markup.

Laura Bennett
Director, Pricing Programs
Redwood Inference
Attachment: pricing_exhibit_markup.docx (pricing suggestions included)
